title: Local-ring criterion for Tor independence of two algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $A,C$ be commutative $R$-algebras, and use Tor groups [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] and tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in a ring $T$, write $T_{\mathfrak p}$ for its localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then the following are equivalent: (i) $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(A,C)=0$ for every $n>0$; (ii) for every pair of primes $\mathfrak p\subset A$, $\mathfrak q\subset C$ with common inverse image $\mathfrak r\subset R$, one has $\operatorname{Tor}^{R_{\mathfrak r}}_n(A_{\mathfrak p},C_{\mathfrak q})=0$ for every $n>0$. Equivalently, the canonical augmentation $A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C\to(A\otimes_RC)[0]$ is an isomorphism in the unbounded derived category of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor computed by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. No Noetherian, finite-generation or flatness hypothesis on these rings or algebras is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08HX, lemma-tor-independent, equivalence (1) and (2); the augmentation formulation is the defining Tor homology calculation.

proof.text: Put $D=A\otimes_R C$ and $T_n=\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(A,C)$. By [lem-kun-derived-module-tor-comparison], $H^{-n}(A[0]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C[0])\cong T_n$ for $n\ge0$, and the positive cohomology is zero. Its simultaneous naturality in the two module variables identifies the actions of multiplication by $a\in A$ and $c\in C$ with their actions on Tor. Hence these identifications respect the commuting factor actions, giving the $D$-module structure used below. For any $A$-algebra $A_1$, $A[0]\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_1[0]\cong A_1[0]$: the single complex $A[0]$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], since $A\otimes_A-$ is the identity and therefore exact. On representatives its tensor is $A\otimes_A A_1\to A_1$, $a\otimes a_1\mapsto aa_1$, with inverse $a_1\mapsto1\otimes a_1$.

source.place: Tags 08HW (lemma-tor-independent-flat), 0DJD (lemma-lemma-tor-independent-flat-compare), and 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism); Tor interpretation from Algebra Tag 00LY (section-tor).

proof.text:
Fix primes $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset C$ contracting to $\mathfrak r\subset R$. Put $R_1=R_{\mathfrak r}$, $A_1=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $C_1=C_{\mathfrak q}$ and $E=A_1\otimes_{R_1}C_1$. All structure maps exist: an element outside $\mathfrak r$ maps outside both $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$, hence becomes invertible. The algebra $A\otimes_R R_1$ is the localization of $A$ at the image of $R\setminus\mathfrak r$: the inverse fraction formulas are $a\otimes(t/s)\mapsto ta/s$ and $a/s\mapsto a\otimes(1/s)$. This also follows by specializing [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] and using tensor symmetry. Its subsequent localization at the image of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ is $A_1$, because a fraction of fractions maps to the same fraction in $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and every denominator outside $\mathfrak p$ has been inverted. The identical formulas with $C,\mathfrak q$ give $C_1$ as a localization of $R_1\otimes_R C$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] verifies all three flatness hypotheses of [lem-sfb-flat-ring-diagram-tensor-cohomology]. Apply that node with $B=C$, $M=A[0]$ and $i=-n$. Step 1 over $R$ and $R_1$, and the displayed tensor-unit identification over $A$, give the canonical isomorphism
$$T_n\otimes_D E\ \cong\ \operatorname{Tor}^{R_{\mathfrak r}}_n(A_{\mathfrak p},C_{\mathfrak q})\qquad(n\ge0).$$

source.place: Tag 08HX (lemma-tor-independent), both uses of Tag 08HW; obtain the 08HW formula by specializing Tag 0DJD to M=A[0]. Localization input: Algebra Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), 00HT (lemma-flat-localization).

proof.text: Assume (i). For each pair of primes in (ii) and each $n>0$, $T_n=0$. Its tensor with $E$ is zero: the tensor product is generated by pure tensors and $0\otimes e=0$. The isomorphism of Step 2 therefore makes $\operatorname{Tor}^{R_{\mathfrak r}}_n(A_{\mathfrak p},C_{\mathfrak q})$ zero. This proves (ii).

Assume (ii), and fix $n>0$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak s\subset D$, let $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$ be its inverse images in $A$ and $C$. They are prime, since the inverse image of a proper prime under a unital ring map is proper and prime; their inverse images in $R$ coincide because $r\otimes1=1\otimes r$. Form $E$ as in Step 2. There is a compatible ring map $E\to D_{\mathfrak s}$: send $a/u$ to $(a\otimes1)/(u\otimes1)$ and $c/v$ to $(1\otimes c)/(1\otimes v)$. The denominators avoid $\mathfrak s$ by the definitions of $\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q$; both maps agree on $R_{\mathfrak r}$. By (ii) and Step 2, $T_n\otimes_D E=0$. Consequently
$$T_n\otimes_D D_{\mathfrak s}\cong (T_n\otimes_D E)\otimes_E D_{\mathfrak s}=0.$$
Here associativity has explicit mutually inverse maps $(t\otimes e)\otimes z\mapsto t\otimes ez$ and $t\otimes z\mapsto(t\otimes1)\otimes z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], with base and first module both $D$, this tensor is the module localization $(T_n)_{\mathfrak s}$ (using symmetry and $D\otimes_D T_n=T_n$). Thus the linear map $0\to T_n$ becomes bijective at every maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-linear-map-bijective-at-maximal-localizations] to conclude that $0\to T_n$ is bijective, so $T_n=0$. Since $n>0$ was arbitrary, (i) follows.

source.place: Tag 08HX (lemma-tor-independent), (2) to (3) to (1); Algebra Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local), using its maximal-localization bijectivity clause on 0 to T_n.

proof.text: Finally consider the canonical augmentation $\epsilon:A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C\to D[0]$. In the Tor definition choose a free resolution $F_\bullet\to A$ and put $F_i$ in cochain degree $-i$. It is bounded above and K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], since its terms are free and tensoring with a free module is a direct sum of copies of the identity. Thus $F_\bullet\otimes_R C$ computes this derived tensor and represents $\epsilon$ by its augmented degree-zero map. Its $H^0$ map is the canonical identification $\operatorname{Tor}^R_0(A,C)=D$ from [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]; there is no positive cochain term, and its degree $-n$ cohomology is $T_n$ for $n>0$, also as in [lem-kun-derived-module-tor-comparison]. Therefore $H^i(\epsilon)$ is an isomorphism for all $i$ exactly when every $T_n$ for $n>0$ vanishes. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] this is equivalent to $\epsilon$ being an isomorphism in the unbounded derived category. This proves the final equivalence without any finiteness or flatness hypothesis on $A$ or $C$.

Step 1: the cited Tor comparison is natural in both variables, which carries the A and C actions over to Tor, and A[0] is K-flat by lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat. Step 2: the flat-diagram node is applied with R_1=R_r, A_1=A_p, B_1=C_q, M=A[0], i=-n. I checked each flatness hypothesis: A tensor R_r is a localisation of A, A_p is a further localisation of it, and the same holds for C. The node's conclusion gives T_n tensor_D E = Tor^{R_r}_n(A_p,C_q), which is the 08HW formula. Step 3 is genuinely elementary. Step 4: the contractions of a maximal ideal s of D are primes over a common prime, the map E->D_s is well defined, (T_n)_s is identified by the localization-tensor node, and the 00HN node applies to 0->T_n; the case D=0 is covered vacuously. Step 5: a free resolution in cochain degrees <=0 is K-flat, H^0 of the augmentation is Tor_0=A tensor C, and the derived-iso criterion finishes the equivalence with the canonical map. Small cases checked: Z/p with Z/p (both sides fail), Z/2 with Z/3 (vacuous, D=0, both sides hold), R[x] (flat, both sides hold). The DAG has no ring-level duplicate and the item does not cycle back on itself. The two tool_uses (Tor comparison, bounded-flat K-flat) are generic homological tools and accepted.
